Download the World Flora Online taxonomic backbone

Source: R/download.R
WFO.download.Rd

Downloads the latest classification.csv of the World Flora Online (WFO) Plant List from Zenodo (https://zenodo.org/records/18007552 and its newer versions), unless a copy is already present. Downloads are verified with the published MD5 checksum and retried with exponential back-off.

Usage

WFO.download(
  WFO.url = NULL,
  save.dir = NULL,
  WFO.remember = TRUE,
  timeout = 3600,
  force = FALSE,
  update = FALSE,
  record.id = "18007552",
  pinned = FALSE,
  ...
)

download_classification(
  out_dir = "wfo_data",
  force = FALSE,
  update = FALSE,
  record_id = "18007552",
  pinned = FALSE
)

Arguments

WFO.url

If given, download a zip archive from this address and extract classification.csv (or classification.txt) instead of using Zenodo.

save.dir, out_dir

Directory for the backbone (created if needed). With save.dir = NULL (default), each release is saved in its own folder of the per-user data folder of WorldFloraFast (see Details and WFO.releases()); save.dir = getwd() gives the default of WorldFlora (the working directory).

WFO.remember

If TRUE, remember the location of the file and load the backbone as WFO.data with WFO.remember().

timeout

Minimum timeout in seconds for the download.

force

If TRUE, download again even if a copy exists.

update

If TRUE and a copy exists, check Zenodo for a newer release and download it if there is one. Without it, an existing copy is used and Zenodo is not contacted. If Zenodo cannot be reached, the local copy is kept with a warning.

record.id, record_id

Zenodo record to start from (any version of the WFO Plant List).

pinned

If TRUE, use record.id itself instead of its newest version.

...

Further arguments for utils::download.file() (with WFO.url only).

Value

The path of the backbone file (invisibly), with attributes version, record_id and doi (NA when unknown).

Details

By default (save.dir = NULL), the backbone is saved in the per-user data folder of WorldFloraFast, given by tools::R_user_dir() (R_user_dir("WorldFloraFast", "data"), subfolder wfo), in a folder named after the release, such as wfo/2026-06/classification.csv. This folder is the same in every session and project, and is kept when the package or R are reinstalled; WFO.releases() lists the releases it holds and deletes old ones. Without update or force, an existing release is used and Zenodo is not contacted (unless pinned = TRUE asks for a given release, which is downloaded to its own folder if needed); with update = TRUE, a newer release is downloaded to a new folder and the older ones are kept. With WFO.url, the file is saved in the subfolder from_url. WorldFlora saved the backbone in the working directory, which save.dir = getwd() still does.

In a new session, WFO.match() without WFO.data or WFO.file, WFO.read() and WFO.remember() use the backbone file of the last download, or else the newest release in the data folder.

Next to the backbone, classification_source.json records the Zenodo record, version, DOI, source file, MD5 checksum and date of the download. A mirror can be used by setting the environment variable ZENODO_BASE; ZENODO_RETRY_WAIT sets the first waiting time (in seconds) between retries.

download_classification() is deprecated: use WFO.download(). It used the argument names of the stand-alone download script, unlike the other functions, and does not remember or load the backbone (WFO.remember = FALSE).

See also

WFO.releases(), WFO.read(), WFO.remember()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# download (or find) the backbone in the data folder, remember it and load it
# as WFO.data
WFO.download()

# in a later session: nothing to download, WFO.match() finds the backbone
WFO.match("Faidherbia albida")

# look for a newer release (kept next to the older ones)
WFO.download(update = TRUE)
WFO.releases()

# a specific release: the WFO Plant List 2026-06
WFO.download(record.id = "20782718", pinned = TRUE)

# another folder, such as a shared drive or the project folder (as in
# WorldFlora)
WFO.download(save.dir = "wfo_data")
} # }
